title: Nutrition risque dans Critically Ill (NUTRIC) score
formula:
Addition of the selected points:

| | Points | | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| Age (years) | <50 | 50–74 | ≥75 | -- |
| [APACHE II](nabda:calc.apache-ii-score\) | <15 | 15–19 | 20–27 | ≥28 |
| [SOFA Score](nabda:calc.sequential-organ-failure-assessment-sofa-score\) * | <6 | 6–9 | ≥10 | -- |
| Number of comorbidities | 0–1 | ≥2 | -- | -- |
| Days in hospital to ICU admit | 0 | ≥1 | -- | -- |
| IL-6 (µ/mL) | 0–399 | ≥400 | -- | -- |

*Initial, on presentation.

how_to_use.why:
- Other risk scores consider all ICU patients to be high risk. The NUTRIC Score identifies patients who are particularly likely to have a mortality benefit from aggressive nutrition therapy.
- Recommended by[American College of Gastroenterology (ACG) guidelines for nutrition therapy](https://www.mdcalc.com/guidelines/acg/nutrition-therapy-adult-hospitalized-patient).
how_to_use.pearls:
- Can be calculated without IL-6, which is not commonly ordered in many ICU settings, without sacrificing significant predictive power.
- Greater predictive power in ICU patients specifically, compared with other nutritional risk scores like [NRS-2002](nabda:calc.nutrition-risk-screening-2002-nrs-2002) .

next_steps.advice: Consider aggressive nutrition therapy (enteral or parenteral) for patients at high risk.

medium_description: Identifies critically ill patients who can benefit de nutrition therapy, recommended par[ACG guidelines](https://www.mdcalc.com/guidelines/acg/nutrition-therapy-adult-hospitalized-patient).
